Respondents consisted of predominantly white and Black/African American respondents, with a smaller representation from Asian, Native Hawaiian, Hispanic, and other racial and ethnic groups. Respondents were largely between 25 and 54 years old. A majority of respondents (87%) indicated that they make decisions about hiring or training workers as part of their job. Almost a third of the companies where respondents worked were woman- and/or minority-owned. Figure 1. Geography of respondents Respondents work in 37 U.S. states; Washington, D.C; Guam; and the Marshall Islands, with the top three primary states of work being California, New York, and Texas. This distribution indicates that the findings are nationally relevant, while also reflecting the concentration of residential energy and building activity (i.e., higher populations) in certain markets. Industry and Building Types Respondents reported working across a variety of industry segments, but many best described themselves as general contractors or as firms providing multiple building services. Specialized trades, such as HVAC/R, insulation, electrical, and weatherization, were also well represented, reflecting the mix of roles in delivering energy performance upgrades. In terms of building types, respondents indicated that they primarily work on commercial and multifamily buildings but also reported substantial activity in residential buildings. This significant overlap suggests that contractors often operate across multiple market segments, which may influence both their hiring needs and training priorities.
